what_it_does: Isolated DC-DC converters are power supplies that provide different output voltages to different parts of a chip while maintaining electrical isolation (no direct current path between sections). When a converter needs to supply multiple isolated domains (different chip regions at different voltages), traditional designs require separate control signals crossing isolation barriers and custom wiring, adding complexity and requiring digital isolators (special chips for sending signals across isolation). This paper presents SLiMDO (Single-Link Multi-Domain-Output), which uses a single communication link and passive magnetic coupling (sharing transformer coils) to control all domains simultaneously. The receiver side senses circuit behavior and adjusts global power modulation accordingly, eliminating the need for multiple control links and digital isolators while still allowing flexible per-domain voltage configuration.
